messages:
Ryan: Quick heads-up — g-12-04 threw Xid 13 twice during a 3h inference run. Low-priority traffic but saw latency spikes. Planning thermal-cycle + extended soak before returning to pool.

Emily: ack. can you paste dmesg + ECC counters? want to see if its memory vs pci/firmware.

Ryan: dmesg snippet:
```
[Mar 10 09:12:05] NVRM: GPU 0000:01:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 13, PID=2245, GPU has fallen off the bus
[Mar 10 09:12:05] nvidia-modeset: GPU120: Fatal GPU exception
```
ECC before/after:
```
gpu:0 correctable: 12 uncorrectable: 0
gpu:1 correctable: 0 uncorrectable: 0
```

Mandeep: Xid 13 often = GPU hang from thermal stress or flaky solder/PCB. thermal cycling is reasonable. also run cuda-memtest and a long small-batch infer loop to exercise kv cache.

QA Bot: Suggested template: 24h idle soak + 48h stress with 3 checkpoints. Run at least one pass in-rack to rule out power/ambient issues.

Emily: proposed concrete plan:
- drain node
- snapshot logs (nv-hostengine, `nvidia-smi -q -x`, dmesg)
- 4h thermal cycle: 20m high load (combined CPU+cuda), 10m cool (fan max -> idle), repeat 6x
- then 72h steady soak at ~65% GPU util
- gating: any Xid w/ uncorrectable ECC or host reboots -> RMA/replace

Chris: for stress I use a small-batch infer loop. quick helper:
```
for i in {1..360}; do
  python3 tests/infer_bench.py --model tiny --batch 8 --seq 1024 --iter 100
  sleep 5
done
```
catches kv-cache issues and mem corruption faster than pure memtest.

Ryan: putting that on the node now. will also capture nvml traces every 30s (nvml poller + `nvidia-smi dmon`) to correlate with dmesg and host logs. uploading dumps to S3.

Mandeep: add ECC gating: if correctable spikes >10/min escalate to hw-replace. watch host PCIe CRC errors (ethtool stats) as well.

Emily: also grab BMC ambient/power telemetry. sometimes reproduces only when inlet temps change. if safe, adjust inlet fans to simulate higher ambient.

Ryan: question: should we flash firmware as part of triage? last fw push was ~2 weeks ago.

Chris: dont flash mid-triage. if we get stable repro, then test firmware on a known-good sibling node to confirm. only change fw in controlled validation.

QA Bot: Checklist saved: /ops/checklists/gpu-thermal-validate — includes log commands and thresholds. :white_check_mark:

Emily: if we hit persistent Xid13 + any uncorrectable ECC after stress, open hw warranty and mark node quarantined.

Ryan: starting drain now. first nvml dump uploaded: s3://redwood-infra/gpu-triage/g-12-04/1782345678/nvml-dump-1.xml

Mandeep: if this passes, keep it on 48h probation in reduced pool for a week. dont return directly to full-production.

Ryan: update: after 12h thermal cycling we saw 2 more Xid13s during high-load windows. ECC remains correctable-only. pushing ticket and RMA.

Emily: ok marking RMA candidate, pinging hardware-team and creating ticket.

ops-bot: Ticket INFRA-4227 created -> Hardware RMA request for g-12-04. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4227

Ryan: notes set in node metadata: quarantine=true, triage_owner=Ryan, triage_started=1782345678

Chris: add metrics to the incident for ML signals: Xid counts, ECC correctable rate, temp distribution, pci crc errs, host reboots. helpful for pattern detection.

Emily: I'll pin a Grafana dashboard to the ticket and add the metric queries.

Ryan: final: we'll add a short on-call how-to to the eng-infra runbook: "thermal-cycle + 72h soak" after RMA outcome. will draft.

Mandeep: thanks all :thumbsup:

Ryan: if anyone wants to repro locally ping me, I'll share the small-batch infer container + nvml poller.
